source_text.body:
Run data research projects with a coding agent
An author used Claude Code on data projects including Canadian daycare research, grading it B- for imperfect reliability and weak research documentation.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
Richard Demsyn-Jones ran Claude Code on three data projects: a sudoku rating algorithm, a Canadian daycare research report, and a SQL analysis tool for work. For the daycare report, he had it search the web, consolidate sources, and build a repeatable report playbook. He pushed it toward organized sources, tiered analysis, and skeptical evaluation criteria.
How it went
The daycare project got a B-. It was a big time saver and he learned the program's basics. But the folder structure got messy, the agent echoed government framing, and the analysis stayed shallow even after several rounds of feedback.
Worth knowing
Give permissions up front and add download caching. Without that, the agent tends to one-shot a web summary and keeps pausing to ask about downloads.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I want to research [topic, e.g. childcare costs in my province] using public data. Find the relevant datasets, download them, clean them, and write analysis scripts that answer [my research question]. Keep a README that records every source, every cleaning step, and any assumption or number you could not verify, so I can check your work. Stop when I have one chart or table answering the question plus that README.
Original source: https://simplicityissota.substack.com/p/claude-code-for-data-work
